# Blanket

The full-screen layer that holds the blanket fill and a modal, so a modal is placed, not drawn. It fills with the blanket, pads 16 at the sides and 64 above and below, centers its child, and sits on the blanket layer (500) with its child on the modal layer (510). With `placement` `start` or `end` it drops the pad and holds its child full height at that edge of the screen, for a drawer. Modal, Drawer and the overlay Panel all draw this one Blanket, so the fill and the layer order are the same under each. The Panel's is `contained`: it covers its Frame, not the screen. It draws the layer only: it does not trap focus, close on Escape or count toward the two-overlay limit. For a real dialog, use the core Modal component, which draws the same layers and blanket token; PatternDrawer brings its own focus handling.

Also asked as: scrim.

**Import:** `import { Blanket } from '@/patterns';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/patterns/Blanket/Blanket.jsx`

## Usage

A Blanket interrupts the page for one task. It dims everything behind it with one fill, so the person sees only the layer on top. It never draws content of its own.

| Layer | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Modal | One task blocks the page. The Blanket centers it. |
| Drawer | The task needs the page in view. The Blanket holds it at an edge. |
| Overlay Panel | The Frame is too narrow to dock the Panel. A `contained` Blanket covers the Frame's Page and Sidebar, with the same fill and layer order as a modal's. |

The Blanket draws the layer only. It does not trap focus, close on Escape or count toward the two-overlay limit. For a real dialog, use the core Modal component, which draws the same layers and blanket token. The Drawer pattern brings its own focus handling. `inline` draws the Blanket in the page flow at a stand-in screen of `screenWidth` and `screenHeight`, for docs and previews.

### Layers

Figma has no z-index, so the order is written here and lives in code.

| Layer | Number | Token | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Navigation | 200 | `--layer-navigation` | The floating sidebar. It has a shadow and no blanket, and an outside click closes it. |
| Menu and Popup | 400 | `--layer-popup` | The Menu and the Popup. One opened from a Modal mounts in it and takes the Modal layer, 510. |
| Blanket | 500 | `--layer-blanket` | The Blanket and its fill. |
| Modal | 510 | `--layer-modal` | A Modal or a Drawer. |
| Flag | 600 | `--layer-flag` | Flags, above a modal. |
| Tooltip | 800 | `--layer-tooltip` | Tooltips, above everything. |

## Content guidelines

The Blanket holds no text of its own. The words belong to the layer it holds.

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title a confirm with the question: "Discard changes?" | A second dialog that repeats the first one's title. |
| Name the confirm's primary action for what it does: "Discard changes". | "OK" or "Yes". |

## Best practices

### Stack only the confirm a layer raises. {#stack-only-the-confirm-a-layer-raises}

A confirm raised from a modal or drawer is a second Blanket over the first. A modal or drawer for another task waits until the first one closes.

Do: A drawer and the confirm it raises, stacked over it.
Don't: A modal for an unrelated task opened over a drawer.

### Never a third overlay. {#never-a-third-overlay}

The overlay module refuses a third: it stays closed and calls its `onClose`.

Do: A modal and its confirm: two overlays.
Don't: A third overlay over a modal and its confirm.

### Confirm in a small modal. {#confirm-in-a-small-modal}

Do: Confirm in a small modal.
Don't: Confirm in a large modal.

Opening a modal closes a floating sidebar, so the two never stack. A floating sidebar gets a shadow and no blanket, and popups, flags and tooltips never bring one.

### Place a modal in the Blanket. {#place-a-modal-in-the-blanket}

Let the Blanket place the modal. Do not detach it to move things around: the pads are the closest a modal gets to the screen edge.

## Accessibility

- The Blanket is a layout layer with no role. The Modal or Drawer inside it is the dialog.
- The blanket is a pointer shortcut, not a control. A keyboard closes a dialog from inside it, so the blanket takes no role and no key handler.
- The blanket at `--ds-blanket` keeps the dialog legible in Light and Dark. The toolbar's Contrast switch changes it with the rest of the page.
- A layer wider than a narrow screen keeps its width, and the Blanket scrolls.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `placement` | enum | `'center'` | `center` (default) for a modal; `start` or `end` holds the layer full height at that edge, with no pad. |
| `inline` | bool | `false` | Draw in the page flow at a stand-in screen, for docs and previews, instead of fixed over the page. |
| `contained` | bool | `false` | Cover the nearest positioned parent instead of the screen, with no pad and no layer inside: the overlay Panel's Blanket over a Frame's Page and Sidebar. The fill and the layer order stay the shared ones. |
| `screenWidth` | number | — | Inline only: the screen width (px) the layers inside take their width from, such as 768, 1024 or 1440. |
| `screenHeight` | number | — | Inline only: the screen height (px); a layer inside caps at it less Blanket/pad-y above and below. The pad follows the real viewport (24 under 640 tall), not this height, as Figma's frames do. |
| `onBlanketClick` | func | — | Called for a click on the blanket, not on the layer it holds. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |
| `children` | node | — | The layer it holds: a PatternModal, a confirm over one, or a drawer at an edge. |

## Variants

**`placement`** — `center` · `start` · `end`

Anything not listed is not a valid value.
